unit.title: Cut, fit and install trunking system

theory1.instructions: Answer all 45 questions. Each question has one best answer: choose it. Each question is worth 1 mark. Time allowed: 2 hours 30 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

questions.stem: Why should you wear gloves when cutting and handling steel trunking?
options: Cut steel edges can be very sharp
Steel trunking is always hot to the touch
Gloves stop the trunking from rusting later
Gloves make the trunking lighter to carry

questions.stem: Before you drill a wall to fix trunking in a building that is in use, what must you check?
options: That the drill bit is the longest one you have
That the wall will be painted again afterwards
That the customer has gone home for the day
That no hidden cables or pipes are there

questions.stem: What should you check before cutting any trunking for a run?
options: The route, sizes and fittings on the drawing
The colour of lid that the customer likes best
Which worker last used the trunking saw
The price of the trunking at a different shop

questions.stem: What is trunking?
options: A round pipe that cables are pulled through
An open ladder that cables are laid across
A closed channel with a removable lid
A flexible tube used for the last metre to a motor

questions.stem: What is one main advantage of trunking over conduit?
options: Trunking never needs to be fixed to the wall
Cables can be laid in and added through the lid
Trunking does not need any earth continuity
Trunking can be buried in the ground without care

questions.stem: Where is dado or skirting trunking with several compartments often used?
options: Under the ground outside, between two buildings
Inside a motor to carry its winding wires
Around office walls, for power and data outlets
In ceilings only, to hold the light fittings

questions.stem: What is small PVC mini-trunking most often used for?
options: Main supply cables from the meter to the board
Large bundles of power cables in a factory
Cables buried under wet ground outdoors
A few cables run on the surface of a room

questions.stem: Which fitting is used where a trunking run turns around the outside of a wall corner?
options: An internal angle
An external angle
A flat tee
An end cap

questions.stem: What is a trunking end cap used for?
options: To close off the open end of a trunking run
To join two lengths of trunking together end to end
To turn the trunking through a 90° corner
To hold the cables in on a vertical run

questions.stem: Which fitting lets one trunking run branch off another at a right angle?
options: A tee
A coupler
An end cap
A reducer

questions.stem: What is a reducer fitting used for?
options: To cut down the number of cables in a run
To join trunking of two different sizes
To reduce the weight of a long vertical run
To lower the voltage of the cables inside

questions.stem: Why should you mark the cut lines on trunking with a square?
options: So the cut line is easier to rub off
So the saw blade lasts longer
So the lid fits loosely after cutting
So the cut is straight across, at 90°

questions.stem: Which tool is commonly used to cut PVC trunking to length?
options: A cold chisel and a mallet
A round pipe cutter
A fine-tooth hacksaw
Heavy-duty side cutters

questions.stem: Why is a mitre box useful when cutting trunking?
options: It holds the lid on while the cables go in
It measures the length of the trunking run
It cools the saw blade as you cut through
It guides the saw for true 45° and 90° cuts

questions.stem: After cutting steel trunking, what must you do to the cut edges?
options: File off all sharp edges and burrs
Paint them bright red so they can be seen
Leave them sharp so the lid grips well
Bend them inward to hold the cables tight

questions.stem: How do you make a neat 90° flat bend in PVC trunking without a factory fitting?
options: Heat the trunking and bend it round by hand
Cut both pieces square and push them together
Cut both pieces at 45° so they meet in a mitre
Overlap the two pieces and screw them together

questions.stem: Why should the joints in the trunking lid be placed away from the joints in the base?
options: So the lid can be taken off in one piece
To make the run stronger and neater
So that water can drain through the gaps
So that fewer fixing screws are needed

questions.stem: How are lengths of steel trunking usually joined?
options: With solvent cement, the same as PVC conduit
With couplers fixed by screws, nuts or rivets
By welding them on site with a stick welder
By tying them together with cable ties

questions.stem: Why are copper earth links fitted across the joints in steel trunking?
options: To hold the joints tight against the wall
To carry the cables across the joint
To keep the earth path unbroken at joints
To stop the lid sliding off along the run

questions.stem: How should the earth continuity of a finished steel trunking run be checked?
options: With a continuity tester, on the dead run
By looking along the run for gaps
By switching on and touching each joint in turn
By knocking on each joint to hear it

questions.stem: How should trunking be fixed to a concrete block wall?
options: With nails knocked into the mortar joints of the wall
With glue only, along the back of the run
With tie wire wrapped round the trunking
With screws into plugs, at the maker's spacing

questions.stem: Why should you use round-head screws with washers to fix PVC trunking?
options: So the screws can be taken out more quickly
So that the screws are easier to see from a long way off
So the screw heads hold the lid on firmly
So the screw heads do not split or crack the base

questions.stem: Why should a trunking run be level or plumb?
options: Level runs are able to hold more cables
The lid will not fit unless it is level
It looks neat and lines up with the room
So that the screws do not need plugs

questions.stem: When should the trunking lid be fitted?
options: Before the cables are laid in, to keep dust out
After the cables are in and have been checked
Never, as the lid is only needed for show
Only on runs that are below 1 m from the floor

questions.stem: Why must trunking lids be fitted securely and all the way along?
options: To protect the cables and keep fingers out
So the trunking can carry more weight on top of it
So that the cables inside stay much cooler
So that the earth links do not have to be fitted

questions.stem: In two-compartment trunking, how should power and data cables be run?
options: In separate compartments, kept apart by the divider
In the same compartment, tied tightly together
Power in the trunking and data on top of the lid
Mixed, as long as the data cables are a different colour

questions.stem: Trunking passes through a fire-rated wall. What must be fitted inside the trunking where it passes through?
options: A larger lid to cover the hole in the wall
An extra earth link on each side of the wall
A fire barrier (fire stop) to seal the opening
Nothing, as long as the lid is fitted

questions.stem: On a long vertical run of trunking, why are cable retainers (pin racks or straps) fitted?
options: To stop the lid from sliding down the run
To keep the cables neat for the photograph
To join the lengths of trunking together
So the cables' weight does not rest on the lid

questions.stem: Why must you not overfill trunking with cables?
options: The lid would then be far too easy to pull off
Cables may overheat, and the lid may crush them
The trunking would need fewer fixing screws
The cable colours would fade in the light

questions.stem: Where cables leave trunking through a hole in the side, what should be fitted?
options: A grommet or bush to protect the cables
A strip of insulating tape stuck round the hole
Nothing, as long as the hole is filed
A cable tie pulled tight at the hole

questions.stem: Which tool makes a clean round hole in the side of steel trunking for a box entry?
options: A cold chisel struck with a hammer
A wood spade or auger bit
A knockout punch or hole saw
A centre punch and mallet

questions.stem: Which tool checks that a long trunking run is horizontal?
options: A try square
A tape measure
A plumb bob
A spirit level

questions.stem: A wall is 4.2 m long. Trunking comes in 3 m lengths. How many lengths are needed for one straight run along the wall?
Why do you allow for the fittings when measuring trunking lengths between corners?
options: Fittings take up part of the length of the run
Fittings make the trunking shrink after fixing
Fittings must always be cut from the trunking
Fittings need an extra 1 m at each end

questions.stem: The drawing gives a height for the outlet trunking. Where should it be fixed?
options: At any height that is easy for you to reach
On the floor, so the outlets are hidden
Just below the ceiling, out of the way
At the drawing height, from finished floor

questions.stem: Why is steel trunking galvanised or painted?
options: So it is lighter to carry and fix
To protect it from rust
So it does not need earthing
To make it bend more easily

questions.stem: Which is a sign of poor trunking work?
options: Tight, neat joints with no gaps
Lids that fit all the way along
Gaps at mitres and sharp edges
Fixings at even spacing along the run

questions.stem: The trunking route on the drawing is now blocked by a new air-conditioning unit. What should you do?
options: Fit the trunking behind the unit anyway
Report it and agree a new route
Run the trunking through the unit's casing
Leave that part of the job for another day

questions.stem: You must add cables to a trunking that already holds working circuits. What must happen first?
options: The circuits are isolated, locked off and proved dead
The lid is taken off quickly while the circuits are still on
You wear rubber gloves and carry on with care
You ask a co-worker to watch the board for you

questions.stem: After proving a circuit dead, why do you check the tester again on a known live source or proving unit?
options: To use up the tester's battery evenly
To show the customer how the tester works
To reset the tester's display to zero
To check the tester did not fail during use

questions.stem: How should a trunking lid be cut where an outlet box or fitting is on the run?
options: Leave a large gap so the cables can be seen
Bend the lid so it sits on top of the box
Cut it neatly to fit close to the fitting
Leave the lid off that section altogether

questions.stem: Why is a fixing placed close to each end of a trunking length?
options: To stop the ends lifting and the joints opening
To make the trunking easier to take down again later
So the middle of the run needs no fixings
So the lid can be clipped on more quickly

questions.stem: How should lengths of PVC trunking be stored on site?
options: Standing up against a wall in the sun
Flat and supported, out of direct sun
Under heavy materials to keep them straight
Outside on the ground, so they stay cool

questions.stem: What should be done with the off-cuts of trunking and lid?
options: Pushed into the trunking behind the cables
Left in the ceiling space for next time
Burnt in the yard at the end of the day
Sorted into the right bins for waste or reuse

questions.stem: Before handing over a trunking run, what should you check?
options: Joints, fixings, lids and earth links
Only that the lid colour matches the wall
That off-cuts are left inside the trunking
That the cables are pulled tight at the bends

theory2.instructions: Section A has 15 short answers (2 marks each). Section B has 10 essay questions (5 marks each): answer each in full sentences. Time allowed: 3 hours 35 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

essays.stem: Describe the hazards when cutting, fitting and installing trunking, and say how you would control each one.
essays.modelAnswer: Cut edges and burrs on steel trunking are very sharp, so I wear gloves and file every edge smooth. Saw dust, metal chips and drilling dust can get into the eyes and lungs, so I wear safety glasses, and a dust mask and ear protection when drilling. Drilling into a wall could hit hidden cables or pipes, so I check the drawings and use a cable detector before drilling. High runs mean work at height, so I use a sound stepladder or platform set up on firm, level ground. Long lengths of trunking can hit people or light fittings when they are carried, so I carry them with a partner. If cables are to be added to trunking that already holds circuits, those circuits must be isolated, locked off, tagged and proved dead first. Off-cuts on the floor are trip hazards, so I clear them as I go.
markingPoints: Sharp edges: gloves and filing
Dust and chips: safety glasses, dust mask, ear protection
Hidden services: check drawings and use a detector
Work at height: sound ladder or platform set up correctly
Existing circuits isolated and proved dead; trips and carrying controlled

essays.stem: Compare PVC trunking and steel trunking. Give two advantages of each, and say where you would use each one.
essays.modelAnswer: PVC trunking is light, cheap and easy to cut with a fine-tooth saw, and its cut edges are not sharp. It does not rust, so it suits damp places and buildings near the sea, and it does not need earthing because it does not conduct. It is used in homes, offices, classrooms and shops, often as mini-trunking or as dado and skirting trunking with outlets. Steel trunking is much stronger and protects cables well against knocks, and it can carry many heavy cables over long runs. It does not soften in heat and stands up better in a fire. It is used in factories, workshops, plant rooms and large buildings. However, it is heavier and harder to cut, its edges must be filed, it can rust unless it is galvanised or painted, and it must be earthed, with earth links across the joints.
markingPoints: PVC: light, cheap, easy to cut
PVC: no rust, no earthing; used in homes, offices, classrooms
Steel: strong protection, carries heavy cable loads
Steel: better in heat and fire; used in factories and workshops
Steel drawbacks: heavier, sharp edges, rust, must be earthed

essays.stem: Describe how you would plan and mark out a trunking run along two walls of a classroom, with one corner.
essays.modelAnswer: I read the drawing to find the size and type of trunking, its height above the floor, the outlet positions and the fittings needed. I measure both walls and the corner, and note any doors, windows, pipes or air-conditioning units in the way. I make a list of the lengths and fittings: straight lengths, an internal angle for the corner, end caps, couplers and outlet boxes. I mark the height of the trunking from the finished floor level at each end of each wall, then use a spirit level or laser to mark a level line, and snap a chalk line along it. I mark where each joint, fitting and outlet will go, and plan the joints so that they are not at outlets. I mark the fixing points at the maker's spacing, with one near each end of every length, and check for hidden services before drilling.
markingPoints: Reads the drawing for size, height, outlets and fittings
Measures the walls and notes obstacles
Lists lengths and fittings, including the corner fitting
Marks a level line from the floor level and snaps a chalk line
Marks joints, outlets and fixings; checks for hidden services

essays.stem: Describe how to cut and fit a mitred 90° flat bend in PVC trunking so that the joint is neat.
essays.modelAnswer: I measure the two lengths that meet at the corner, measuring to the inside or outside edge as the drawing needs. I mark a 45° line across the base of each piece where it is to be cut. I put the first piece in a mitre box with the base flat, and cut along the 45° slot with a fine-tooth saw, keeping the saw upright and using steady strokes. I cut the second piece the same way but at the opposite 45°, so the two ends make a right angle. I remove any burrs with a file or knife. I hold the two pieces together on the wall to check the fit, and adjust if there is a gap. Then I fix both pieces close to the joint so it stays tight. I cut the lid pieces the same way so the lid mitre sits over the base mitre, and check that the lids clip on neatly.
markingPoints: Measures and marks 45° lines accurately
Uses a mitre box and fine-tooth saw with steady, upright strokes
Cuts the second piece at the opposite angle
Deburrs and dry-fits, correcting any gap
Fixes close to the joint and mitres the lid to match

essays.stem: Describe how to fix a length of trunking to a block wall so that it is straight, level and secure.
essays.modelAnswer: I hold the trunking base on the level chalk line and mark the fixing holes through it, at the maker's fixing spacing, with one fixing near each end. I take the trunking down and check for hidden cables and pipes. I drill the wall with a masonry bit of the right size in a hammer drill, wearing safety glasses, a dust mask and ear protection. For steel trunking, I also drill or punch holes in the base if there are none. I push in wall plugs that suit the screws. I fix the trunking with round-head or pan-head screws and washers, so the heads sit flat and do not crack the PVC or catch the cables. I check with a spirit level that the trunking is level along its length, and that the joint with the next length is tight and in line, before I fit the next piece.
markingPoints: Marks fixings on the level line at the maker's spacing, one near each end
Checks for hidden services and wears PPE when drilling
Uses wall plugs that suit the screws
Uses round-head or pan-head screws with washers
Checks level and tight, in-line joints

essays.stem: Describe how cables should be laid into a trunking run and the lid fitted, so that the cables are safe and easy to work on later.
essays.modelAnswer: Before laying cables, I check that all joints are tight, sharp edges are filed and grommets or bushes are fitted where cables leave the trunking. Any circuits already in the trunking must be isolated, locked off and proved dead. I lay the cables in neatly, side by side, without twisting them or crossing them more than needed. Power cables go in their own compartment, and data and telephone cables go in a separate compartment, behind the divider. I do not overfill the trunking, so the cables stay cool and the lid fits without pressing on them. On vertical runs, I fit cable retainers so the cables' weight is not on the lid. I label circuits where they enter and leave. Finally I fit the lid all the way along, starting at one end, and make sure it clips on fully.
markingPoints: Checks joints, edges and grommets; isolates any existing circuits
Lays cables neatly without twisting
Keeps power and data in separate compartments
Does not overfill; fits retainers on vertical runs
Labels circuits and fits the lid fully

essays.stem: Describe how to join two lengths of steel trunking and fit a tee, including the earth links.
essays.modelAnswer: I cut the lengths square with a hacksaw, file off all burrs and sharp edges, and wear gloves and safety glasses. I butt the two lengths together on the wall, in line and level. I fit a coupler inside or over the joint and fix it with the screws, nuts or rivets supplied, so the joint is tight and does not move. For the tee, I fit the factory tee piece into the run, or cut the side of the main run neatly for the branch as the maker says, and fix it with its couplers. Across each joint I fit a copper earth link, bolted to the trunking on each side with clean metal-to-metal contact, so the earth path is not broken. Finally I check the earth continuity of the run with a low-resistance ohmmeter on the dead system, record the reading, and fit the lids.
markingPoints: Cuts square, files edges, wears gloves and glasses
Fits couplers so the joint is tight and in line
Fits the tee as the maker says
Fits a copper earth link across every joint with clean contact
Tests continuity on the dead run, records it and fits lids

essays.stem: Name five trunking fittings and describe what each one is used for.
essays.modelAnswer: An internal angle is used where the trunking turns around the inside of a wall corner, and an external angle where it turns around the outside of a corner. A flat angle, or flat bend, turns the run through 90° on the same flat surface, for example along a wall and then up it. A tee lets a branch leave the main run at a right angle. An end cap closes the open end of a run, so the cables are covered and dust and insects are kept out. A coupler joins two straight lengths end to end, and a reducer joins trunking of two different sizes. A box adaptor or outlet box lets an accessory, such as an outlet or a switch, be fitted on the trunking. Using the right factory fitting keeps the run neat and protects the cables.
markingPoints: Internal and external angles described correctly
Flat angle or tee described correctly
End cap described correctly
Coupler or reducer described correctly
Box adaptor or outlet box described correctly

essays.stem: Describe how you would inspect a finished trunking installation before handing it over.
essays.modelAnswer: I compare the installation with the drawing to check the route, size, height and outlet positions. I check that the trunking is straight, level and plumb, and that every length is firmly fixed, with fixings near each end and at the right spacing. I look at every joint, mitre and fitting for gaps, and make sure all cut edges are smooth. I check that the lids are fitted all the way along and clip on fully, with neat cuts at fittings and outlets. Inside, I check that the cables are laid neatly and not overfilled, with power and data in separate compartments and retainers on vertical runs. On steel trunking, I check that earth links are fitted across every joint and that the continuity result is recorded. I check that fire barriers are fitted where the run passes through fire walls, that labels are in place and that the area is clean.
markingPoints: Checks against the drawing
Straight, level, plumb and firmly fixed
Joints and mitres tight; edges smooth; lids fully fitted
Cables neat, not overfilled, segregated, supported
Earth links, continuity record, fire barriers, labels and clean area

essays.stem: Explain why trunking work must be kept tidy and the work area cleaned during and after the job, and say how waste should be handled.
essays.modelAnswer: A tidy work area is a safe one. Off-cuts of trunking and lid, and screws on the floor, can make people trip or slip, and sharp steel off-cuts can cut hands and feet. Keeping tools and materials in one place stops them being lost, damaged or stolen, and saves time. In a building that people are using, such as an office or a classroom, the customer expects the area to be left clean, and dust and mess can damage computers and furniture. During the job, I sweep up often and keep materials stacked neatly, out of the sun. At the end, I sort the waste: clean PVC and steel off-cuts go for reuse or recycling where possible, and the rest goes into the right bins. I never leave off-cuts inside the trunking or in the ceiling, and I never burn PVC, because it gives off toxic fumes.
markingPoints: Prevents trips, slips and cuts
Stops loss, damage and wasted time
Protects the customer's building and equipment
Cleans during and after the job; stores materials properly
Sorts waste for reuse or the right bins; never in trunking; never burns PVC

practical1.title: Cut, fit and install a PVC trunking run with angles, a tee and a mitred bend
practical1.brief: On a training bay, the group installs a run of PVC trunking (for example 50 × 50 mm, or the size the assessor gives) along two walls of the bay, as the assessor's drawing shows. The run must include an internal angle at the corner, a flat tee with a short branch, a site-made mitred 90° flat bend cut in a mitre box, an external angle around a pillar or box-out, a coupler joint, an end cap and one outlet box on the trunking. Each member must, while the assessor watches, measure, mark and cut at least one length or mitre, and fix at least one length level on the wall. Lay a short length of cable in to check the fit, then fit all the lids. The bay has no supply. Photograph each stage below and add the photos to the group's practical. Hand in once for the whole group when the run is finished and the area is clean.
materials: PVC trunking and lid (for example 50 × 50 mm), with internal and external angles, flat tee, coupler, end cap and outlet box
Fine-tooth hacksaw or junior hacksaw, mitre box and file
Tape measure, try square, spirit level, chalk line and marker
Hammer drill, masonry bit, wall plugs, round-head screws and washers (or the bay's fixing board)
A short length of cable for a fit check
Safety glasses, dust masks and ear protection
photos: The level line and fixing points marked on the wall
A length being cut square, with the cut line marked
The mitre being cut in the mitre box
The mitred bend fitted on the wall, showing a tight joint
The internal angle, external angle and tee fitted
The trunking fixed level, checked with a spirit level
The finished run with lids, end cap and outlet box fitted
The work area cleaned, with off-cuts in the bin
checklist: Read the drawing and marked a level line at the right height
Measured, marked and cut lengths square, allowing for fittings
Cut a neat 45° mitre in the mitre box, with no gap at the joint
Removed burrs and rough edges from all cuts
Checked for hidden services, then drilled and plugged correctly
Fixed lengths level with round-head screws and washers, with a fixing near each end
Fitted the angles, tee, coupler, end cap and outlet box neatly and tightly
Fitted lids fully along the run and left the area clean
safety: Wear safety glasses when cutting and drilling; add a dust mask and ear protection for drilling
Check for hidden cables and pipes with a detector before drilling
Use a sound stepladder set up on firm, level ground; never stand on the top step
Hold work firmly in the mitre box and keep fingers clear of the saw
The bay has no supply; follow the maker's instructions and the Centre's rules

practical2.title: Install steel trunking with couplers, earth links, a tee, a box entry and a vertical drop
practical2.brief: On a training bay, the group installs a run of galvanised steel trunking (for example 75 × 75 mm, or the size the assessor gives) along a wall, with a tee and a vertical drop to an outlet box, as the assessor's drawing shows. Each member must, while the assessor watches, cut and file at least one length or lid, fit at least one coupler with its earth link, and fix at least one length. The group punches or cuts one hole for a box entry and fits a grommet or bush, fits a conduit adaptor where the drawing shows, and fits cable retainers on the vertical drop. Lay a short length of cable in each compartment to check the fit. When it is finished, check the earth continuity from end to end with a low-resistance ohmmeter or multimeter, and record the reading. The bay has no supply. Photograph each stage below and add the photos to the group's practical. Hand in once for the whole group.
materials: Galvanised steel trunking and lid, with tee, couplers, end caps and copper earth links
Hacksaw with a fine-tooth blade, files and a deburring tool
Knockout punch or hole saw, grommets or bushes, and a conduit adaptor
Cable retainers for the vertical drop
Rivet gun and rivets, or nuts and bolts, as the maker supplies
Tape measure, try square, spirit level and marker
Hammer drill, masonry bit, wall plugs and screws (or the bay's fixing board)
Safety glasses, cut-resistant gloves, dust masks and ear protection
photos: A member cutting a length, wearing gloves and safety glasses
A cut edge after filing, with no burrs
A coupler fitted with its copper earth link
The tee fitted into the run
The box entry hole with its grommet or bush, and the conduit adaptor
The vertical drop with cable retainers fitted
The earth continuity test from end to end
The finished run with lids fitted, and the clean work area
checklist: Measured and cut lengths square, allowing for fittings
Filed all cut edges smooth, wearing gloves and safety glasses
Fitted couplers tightly so the lengths are in line
Fitted a copper earth link across every joint with clean metal contact
Made a neat box entry with a grommet or bush fitted
Fitted cable retainers on the vertical drop
Fixed the run level and plumb at the maker's spacing
Checked earth continuity on the dead run, recorded the reading and left the area clean
safety: Wear cut-resistant gloves and safety glasses when cutting, filing and handling steel trunking
Check for hidden cables and pipes before drilling, and wear a dust mask and ear protection
Carry long lengths with a partner and watch for people and light fittings
Use a sound stepladder or platform for high work
The bay has no supply; follow the maker's instructions and the Centre's rules
